Revised assessment incorporating academic insights:
- The phrase “continued to expand at a solid pace” is clearly positive on real activity. In New Keynesian policy frameworks (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), stronger activity implies a positive output gap that ordinarily calls for tighter policy relative to neutral (consistent with Taylor-rule prescriptions). That hawkish implication tempers the net positivity of the language.
- Communication research on forward guidance (Svensson and Woodford) emphasizes that such phrasing signals confidence in growth and helps anchor expectations; however, when inflation is still above target, upbeat growth language can shift perceived policy-path expectations toward “higher-for-longer,” which markets often read as less dovish.
- Inflation-at-risk perspectives (e.g., recent work highlighting asymmetric inflation risks) suggest robust activity may tilt near-term inflation risks to the upside, again moderating the positive tone for a policy statement.

Net: mildly positive economic tone, tempered by hawkish policy implications.
